h1: The 7 Best Portable Dishwashers Under $500 for Small Kitchens, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 countertop dishwashers under $500, compared on tank vs hookup, programs, noise, capacity and Energy Star status.
summary: The COMFEE' 8-program Energy Star model is the best all-round countertop dishwasher here, while the COMFEE' Mini with its 1.32-gallon tank is the one to buy if you have no faucet access. NOVETE suits parents with its Baby Care cycle, and EUHOMY is the quietest listed at 40dB. AIRMSEN covers slim counters but publishes the least data.
intro: The mistake most buyers make is comparing countertop dishwashers by price alone. At this budget nearly every unit costs about the same, so the real decision is how water gets in: a built-in tank you fill by hand, or a hose to your faucet. Pick wrong and the machine sits in the box, because nobody keeps refilling a tank every night.

We ranked seven models under $500 from their listings and spec data, covering water supply, program count, wash temperature, noise rating and capacity. Where a listing leaves a spec out, we say so rather than guess, and you will see that flagged on the lower-ranked AIRMSEN picks. If your kitchen has a faucet near the counter, favor a hookup; if not, favor a tank.

products.name: COMFEE' 8-Program Energy Star Countertop Dishwasher
products.verdict: Energy Star rating and eight programs make this the most complete countertop washer in the set.
products.description:
The COMFEE' 6-place-setting countertop model is the only unit here that pairs Energy Star certification with eight programs, including Speed, Baby-Care, ECO and Glass. That is a rare spread at a budget this size, and it matters because a countertop washer lives or dies on whether its short cycle actually cleans a dinner for two.

It ranks first over the other COMFEE listings because the program list is the longest and the Glass cycle gives delicate stemware a gentler pass. The mini COMFEE below it adds a built-in tank and a 162°F wash, which solves a different problem, plumbing. This one assumes you will connect it to a faucet, and that is the real tradeoff.

Buy it if you have a sink faucet within reach and want certified efficiency. Skip it if your rental has no usable faucet adapter, since the listing does not advertise a tank.
products.idealFor: Small households with a faucet nearby who want certified efficiency and cycle choice.
products.skipIf: You rent a place with no sink adapter and need a tank-fed unit.

products.name: COMFEE' Portable Mini Countertop Dishwasher
products.verdict: A 1.32-gallon tank and a 162°F wash cycle mean you can run it anywhere with an outlet.
products.description:
The COMFEE' Portable Mini carries its own 1.32-gallon water tank, so there is no plumbing at all: fill, load, press start. It adds six programs, 360 degree dual spray arms, a 162°F high-temperature wash and an air-dry step.

It sits just behind the 8-program model because it drops Energy Star on the listing and trades program count for freedom. That freedom is why it ranks above every other tank-fed pick here: the high-temperature rinse is the one spec that addresses grease and sanitizing in a tank design, where reheating is the usual weak spot.

Choose it for RVs, dorms, and apartments where the faucet is not an option. Refilling is the cost. A tank of this size means you top up the water by hand for every load, so it suits one to two people, not a family.
products.idealFor: RV, dorm and apartment users with no faucet connection.
products.skipIf: You cook for four or more and want fewer refills.

products.name: NOVETE 5L Compact Countertop Dishwasher
products.verdict: A 5L tank with an optional inlet hose, plus a dedicated baby-care cycle.
products.description:
The NOVETE is the flexible one: a 5L built-in tank for no-hookup use, plus an inlet hose if you would rather plumb it in. It runs five programs including a Baby Care cycle, has air-dry and an LED indicator light.

It ranks third because the dual water supply is the best design idea in the group. Tank mode gets you started anywhere, and hose mode removes the refill chore later. It loses ground to COMFEE on program count, with five against six or eight.

Parents are the obvious buyers, since bottle and pacifier sanitizing is what the Baby Care program targets. No place-setting count appears on the listing, so measure your bottles and plates against the interior before you buy.
products.idealFor: Parents sanitizing bottles who may switch between tank and tap.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed place-setting count.

products.name: AIRMSEN Large Slim Countertop Dishwasher
products.verdict: A slim body with a larger interior and a built-in tank, aimed at fitting more per load.
products.description:
The AIRMSEN Large Slim is built around one claim: more interior capacity in a narrower footprint, with a built-in water tank so it needs no hookup. The listing frames it as the largest countertop-class unit at this budget.

It ranks fourth because capacity is the headline, but the specs stop there. There is no program count, temperature or Energy Star mark in the data, so we cannot confirm cycle depth the way we can for the COMFEE picks. The footprint is the selling point on a crowded counter.

Buy it if counter depth is your limiter and you wash bulkier pots. Without published cycle details, check the manual's program list before you commit to a unit that has to replace hand washing.
products.idealFor: Tight counters where a slim body is the deciding factor.
products.skipIf: You want documented cycles and temperatures.

products.name: EUHOMY 40dB 6-Program Countertop Dishwasher
products.verdict: Rated at 40dB with six programs, which suits open-plan and studio living.
products.description:
The EUHOMY countertop unit lists a 40dB noise rating, six wash programs and 360 degree spray coverage in a no-hookup design. Noise is the spec that decides whether a countertop washer is livable in a studio.

It ranks fifth because quiet is its one clear edge and the rest of the data is thin. 40dB is roughly library-level on paper, which beats what most listings in this group disclose at all. Against the COMFEE mini it gives up the stated 162°F wash and the tank volume.

It is the right pick for a one-room apartment where the machine runs near your bed or desk. Decibel ratings come from the maker, so read owner feedback on cycle noise before relying on the number.
products.idealFor: Studio and open-plan renters sensitive to machine noise.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed tank capacity or high-temp wash.

products.name: AIRMSEN No-Hookup Portable Dishwasher
products.verdict: A no-hookup, built-in tank design for people who want it running in minutes.
products.description:
The second AIRMSEN is the stripped-down option. It skips plumbing by using an onboard reservoir, sits on the counter, and sells itself on simple setup. The listing stresses a bigger capacity than entry-level rivals.

It lands last because the published specs are the thinnest in the ranking. No program count, no wash temperature, no noise figure. That is not a flaw in the machine so much as a gap in what we can verify.

Buy it if you want the least fiddly installation and plan to wash everyday dishes rather than pans. Unknowns are risk, so compare it against the COMFEE mini, which spells out its 162°F cycle and tank volume for similar money.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers who want to plug in and go.
products.skipIf: You compare machines on documented specs.

products.name: EUHOMY 6-Program No-Hookup Dishwasher
products.verdict: Six programs and a 40dB listing, for buyers keeping well under the $500 ceiling.
products.description:
The second EUHOMY is a plain countertop washer with six programs, a 40dB listed noise level and no plumbing hookup. It is the sibling of the 360 degree spray model above, with less detail on the spray hardware.

It ranks sixth because it matches the quieter EUHOMY on noise and program count but does not advertise the spray pattern. Choosing between them is mostly a price call, and the listing positions this one as the cheaper way to stay under budget.

Buy it for a spare kitchen, a guest house or a student flat. Tank size and wash temperature are not published, so assume modest capability and run it with pre-scraped plates.
products.idealFor: Spare kitchens and student flats on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want spray design or temperature specifics.

methodology.title: Water supply
methodology.description: Tank, hose or both, and how much refilling a normal load needs.

methodology.title: Cycle depth
methodology.description: Program count and whether a hot wash or Glass cycle is listed.

methodology.title: Noise
methodology.description: Published dB rating, weighed against how open your living space is.

methodology.title: Capacity and footprint
methodology.description: Stated place settings and counter size.

methodology.title: Verifiable specs
methodology.description: Credit for what the listing actually documents, such as Energy Star.

whatMatters.detail: The water supply decides whether the machine fits your life. A built-in tank means you pour water in and need no plumbing, but you refill every load. A hose hookup connects to a faucet adapter and removes the chore, but you need the faucet within reach. Check whether the listing names a tank volume, like the COMFEE' Mini's 1.32 gallons, or an inlet hose, like the NOVETE's.

Wash temperature decides how well it handles grease. Hot water dissolves fats and dried food, while cold-fill tanks struggle with pans and plates. A listed 162°F high-temp wash, as on the COMFEE' Mini, signals the unit heats its own water. If a listing gives no temperature, assume a basic heater, and treat the EUHOMY and AIRMSEN picks accordingly.

Capacity is counted in place settings, and six is the common countertop size. That fits a couple's dinner, not a family's, and large pots rarely fit at all. Compare the stated number with how many plates, bowls and glasses you use in one evening. A capacity that is too small means two cycles a night, which cancels the time you hoped to save.

Noise is measured in decibels, and around 40dB, as EUHOMY lists, is quiet enough for an open room. A countertop machine sits at ear level in a small kitchen, so a loud cycle is hard to ignore. Treat a maker rating as a best case, since no independent figure backs it. Check for a stated dB value, and read owner comments for the real sound.

Energy Star certification means the washer meets set efficiency standards for water and power. Only the COMFEE' 8-program model lists it here. It is a quick check when other specs are thin and a real running-cost signal if you wash daily. Look for the mark in the listing itself, not in the marketing copy, and treat its absence as unknown rather than bad.

cards.text: You fill it by hand and place it anywhere with power. Picks: COMFEE' Mini, AIRMSEN Large Slim, AIRMSEN No-Hookup.

cards.text: Water flows from your tap, so no refilling. Picks: COMFEE' 8-program, NOVETE with its inlet hose.

howToChoose.note: Default to a hookup-capable unit if you own your kitchen, and a tank if you rent.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A built-in tank, a footprint that fits your counter, and no permanent modification. A listed high-temp wash is a bonus.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: COMFEE' Portable Mini for most renters, AIRMSEN Large Slim if counter space is tight.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want certified efficiency and more programs for daily use. The COMFEE' 8-program model is the one to stretch for.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The machine is for occasional use or a second home. The AIRMSEN No-Hookup or EUHOMY covers the basics.

faq.q: Can I use these without plumbing?
faq.a: Yes for the tank models. The COMFEE' Mini holds 1.32 gallons and the NOVETE has a 5L tank, so both run from an outlet alone. The COMFEE' 8-program model is not advertised with a tank, so plan a faucet connection for it.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Assuming every countertop dishwasher cleans like a full-size one. Scrape plates first and load by the stated place settings, six on the COMFEE' models, or results suffer. Large pots and sheet pans will not fit, so wash those by hand.

faq.q: Is this worth it over hand washing?
faq.a: For one to two people, usually yes, if you value the time. The Energy Star COMFEE' saves effort at modest running cost, but a tank model like the COMFEE' Mini still needs refilling by hand every load, which trims the benefit.

faq.q: How do I set up a tank model?
faq.a: Place it on a level counter near an outlet, fill the tank to the marked line, load dishes and pick a program. With the NOVETE you can instead attach the inlet hose to a faucet adapter, which avoids refilling.

Run an empty hot cycle with a descaler every month or two, wipe the door seal and clean the filter. Hard water scale hits tank units like the COMFEE' Mini and AIRMSEN Large Slim first, so use filtered water if yours is hard.

faq.q: Will it be loud at night?
faq.a: The EUHOMY lists 40dB, the only noise rating here, and it is the best choice for a studio. Others do not publish figures, so assume typical dishwasher noise and avoid running them where you sleep or work.

finalTake: The COMFEE' 8-program Energy Star unit is the pick for most buyers with a faucet, and the COMFEE' Mini is the one to buy if you rent or live in an RV. NOVETE handles parents well and EUHOMY is the quiet choice. Treat the AIRMSEN pair as slim-counter options and check their manuals before you buy.
